issues.legal_issue: A pending eviction suit is maintainable when the authority that revoked the original permission is later overruled and the restored permission becomes effective before the decree is passed.
material_facts: The landlord obtained permission to institute an eviction suit and filed the suit.
The Commissioner later revoked that permission.
During the proceedings, the State Government set aside the revocation and directed that the permission would become effective after a specified period.
The suit remained pending, and the trial court passed its decree after the restored permission had become effective.
issues.conclusion: Setting aside the Commissioner’s revocation restored the original permission, and because that permission was effective when the decree was passed, the suit was maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3(1), 3(3), 3(4), and 7F of the U.P. (Temp.) Control of Rent and Eviction Act, 1947, the State Government may set aside the Commissioner’s order revoking permission, thereby restoring the original permission. Where the Government directs that permission take effect later, the suit is maintainable if permission is effective when the decree is passed. Bhagwan Das v. Paras Nath is distinguishable: there, a suit validly instituted with the Commissioner’s permission was not rendered incompetent by a later Government revocation, because the Government’s power to revoke was exhausted after valid institution.

rule.if: eviction_suit and original_permission_granted and commissioner_revoked_permission and government_set_aside_revocation and restored_permission_effective_before_decree

predicates.eviction_suit: A landlord brought a suit seeking eviction of a tenant.
predicates.original_permission_granted: The relevant authority granted permission to institute the suit before it was filed.
predicates.commissioner_revoked_permission: An appellate administrative authority revoked the original permission after the suit was filed.
predicates.government_set_aside_revocation: A higher government authority set aside the administrative revocation and restored the original permission.
predicates.restored_permission_effective_before_dec: The restored permission became effective before the court passed its decree in the still-pending suit.
predicates.suit_is_maintainable: The suit may proceed to judgment and support a decree.

issues.definition: When a landlord’s eviction suit was filed with permission, that permission was revoked but restored by a higher authority, and the restored permission was effective before the decree, the suit is maintainable.
